newsitem.title: UK: LME closes mostly lower, summer slumbers prevail.
newsitem.headline: LME closes mostly lower, summer slumbers prevail.

text.p: Trading conditions remained slow during Monday afternoon LME rings and kerb sessions, with prices gradually crumbling, albeit in low volume.
Traders said the pattern of trading was not unusual for the summer, with little taking place in physicals.
"There is not much you can say about it today. Most of the traders seem content to hold fire. Maybe they're watching things like gold," one analyst said.
Copper just about managed to hold close to the $2,400, with dips being supported, and last trade was at $2,399, down $6.50 from Friday's kerb close.
The market paid little attention to the start of an indefinite strike at Portugal's Neves Corvo mine. Output is seen dropping to 20 percent of normal immediately.

Tightness from next week's July date to the end of the month did induce caution, although there was some general lending interest from midsession onwards, with cash/threes showing a slightly softer $132/142 backwardation at the close.

Aluminium was affected by the slippage in copper, with the market losing grip around $1,600, and confirming the decline during the afternoon. Prices closed at $1,587, down $20, and may now head towards $1,550.
Nickel was unable to hold the $6,900 level, having earlier lacked the drive to re-challenge $7,000, and prices fell away during the afternoon to close at $$6,860, down $130.

Lead also backtracked during the afternoon, having lacked follow through to initial three-month peaks. The downturn partly reflected the general trend, but also a pause after what was a substantial run-up on Friday.
Last business was at $654, down from the $669 peak, and a $10 loss from Friday.
Zinc similarly lost ground, with some of the heat having deserted the market since prices hit 6-3/4 year highs last week. Final trade was at $1,456, a $14 decline from the previous kerb.
Tin was quiet throughout, and closed at an unchanged $5,550 a tonne. Alloy was indicated slightly lower at $1,440/45.
